```yaml
name: PR Delta Validation

on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  validate-delta:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Ensure origin/main is up to date
        run: git fetch origin main

      - name: Install Salesforce CLI
        run: npm install -g @salesforce/cli

      - name: Install sfdx-git-delta plugin
        run: sf plugins install sfdx-git-delta --force

      - name: Generate delta manifest and sources
        run: |
          mkdir -p changed-sources
          sf sgd source delta --from origin/main --to HEAD --output-dir changed-sources --generate-delta

      - name: Authenticate to production
        run: |
          echo "${{ secrets.SF_JWT_KEY }}" > server.key
          sf org login jwt --instance-url https://login.salesforce.com \
            --client-id "${{ secrets.SF_CONSUMER_KEY }}" \
            --username "${{ secrets.SF_USERNAME }}" \
            --jwt-key-file server.key --alias prod
          rm server.key

      - name: Validate deployment with destructive changes
        run: |
          sf project deploy validate \
            --target-org prod \
            --source-dir changed-sources \
            --post-destructive-changes changed-sources/destructiveChanges/destructiveChanges.xml \
            --test-level RunLocalTests \
            --wait 120
```

Key points:

- `--output-dir` replaces the deprecated `--output` flag.
- Deploying with `--source-dir changed-sources` (which contains only the added/changed files produced by `--generate-delta`) avoids the invalid combination of `--manifest` and `--source-dir` in a single command.
- `--post-destructive-changes` points at the `destructiveChanges.xml` sfdx-git-delta generated for deleted components, so deletions are processed after the other components deploy.
- `--wait 120` waits up to 120 minutes; a failed validation exits non-zero and fails the workflow.

```apex
public with sharing class ContactEmailMatcher {

    public class Request {
        @InvocableVariable(required=true)
        public String email;
    }

    public class Result {
        @InvocableVariable
        public Id contactId;
    }

    @InvocableMethod(label='Match Contact by Email')
    public static List<Result> match(List<Request> requests) {
        List<Result> results = new List<Result>();
        if (requests == null || requests.isEmpty()) {
            return results;
        }

        // Normalize emails and collect distinct non-blank values
        Set<String> emails = new Set<String>();
        List<String> normalized = new List<String>();
        for (Request req : requests) {
            String norm = (req != null && req.email != null)
                ? req.email.trim().toLowerCase()
                : '';
            normalized.add(norm);
            if (String.isNotBlank(norm)) {
                emails.add(norm);
            }
        }

        // One SOQL query: earliest-created contact per email
        Map<String, Id> emailToContactId = new Map<String, Id>();
        if (!emails.isEmpty()) {
            List<Contact> contacts = [
                SELECT Id, Email
                FROM Contact
                WHERE Email != null
                ORDER BY CreatedDate ASC, Id ASC
            ];
            for (Contact c : contacts) {
                String key = c.Email.trim().toLowerCase();
                if (emails.contains(key) && !emailToContactId.containsKey(key)) {
                    emailToContactId.put(key, c.Id);
                }
            }
        }

        for (String norm : normalized) {
            Result r = new Result();
            if (String.isNotBlank(norm)) {
                r.contactId = emailToContactId.get(norm);
            }
            results.add(r);
        }
        return results;
    }
}
```

```apex
public with sharing class TA_Opportunity_CollectForErpSync
    implements TriggerAction.AfterInsert, TriggerAction.AfterUpdate {

    /**
     * Ids of opportunities that need to be synced to the ERP in the current
     * DML operation. Because the trigger runs in chunks (200 + 50 for a 250
     * record insert), the set is static so that every chunk of the same DML
     * operation accumulates into it. The DML finalizer consumes it once, at
     * the end of the DML operation.
     */
    private static Set<Id> opportunityIdsToSync = new Set<Id>();

    public void afterInsert(List<SObject> triggerNew) {
        for (SObject record : triggerNew) {
            opportunityIdsToSync.add(record.Id);
        }
    }

    public void afterUpdate(List<SObject> triggerNew, List<SObject> triggerOld) {
        for (Integer i = 0; i < triggerNew.size(); i++) {
            Opportunity newRecord = (Opportunity) triggerNew[i];
            Opportunity oldRecord = (Opportunity) triggerOld[i];
            if (newRecord.StageName != oldRecord.StageName) {
                opportunityIdsToSync.add(newRecord.Id);
            }
        }
    }

    /**
     * Returns the collected Ids and clears the collection, so that the next
     * DML operation in the same transaction starts with an empty set and
     * therefore produces its own, separate job.
     */
    public static Set<Id> consumeOpportunityIdsToSync() {
        Set<Id> consumed = opportunityIdsToSync;
        opportunityIdsToSync = new Set<Id>();
        return consumed;
    }
}
```

```apex
public with sharing class OpportunityErpSyncFinalizer implements TriggerAction.DmlFinalizer {

    /**
     * Called by the framework at the end of every DML operation it handles,
     * for any sObject. This finalizer only acts when the collect action has
     * actually accumulated opportunity Ids during that DML operation; when the
     * set is empty (no relevant opportunity trigger fired), it does nothing.
     *
     * Consuming (and thereby clearing) the set guarantees exactly one job per
     * DML operation, carrying all Ids of that operation across trigger chunks,
     * while separate DML statements each get their own job.
     *
     * Finalizers must not perform DML; enqueueing an asynchronous job is the
     * intended side effect of this pattern.
     */
    public void execute(FinalizerHandler.Context context) {
        Set<Id> opportunityIds = TA_Opportunity_CollectForErpSync.consumeOpportunityIdsToSync();
        if (!opportunityIds.isEmpty()) {
            System.enqueueJob(new OpportunityErpSyncJob(opportunityIds));
        }
    }
}
```
